original_statement:
What must hold? State the invariant or expectation this concerns. Each open site carries its declaration index in source order. The Core keeps the open sites sorted by (declaration index, bytes to the declaration end), so the head site is the source-earliest error. Decisions X1, X2 and X6 and the S1a acceptance check of docs/parallel.md hold.
What holds now? Describe the current, observed state. LeanMend/Core/Mend.lean keeps the open sites in Lean's message order. In EVMLean run 20, Semantics site 1040 was the head site while site 288, earlier in the file, was open. The branch s1-partial (commit 5885691) holds the captured work of the first S1 worker (lea-e1b), killed at the 3600-second task timeout. It builds, it has no sorry, and lake test reports 0 failed. It has Site.declIndex, Site.key, keyLt with its order theorems, Mending.sortOpens with its proofs, Mending.afterCoord, and a five-tuple Mending.measure. It has no tests/order.sh, no tests/expose.sh and no fixture.
How do you see it? Describe exactly how to observe this for yourself — the steps to reproduce, or how you would demo it. Run tests/order.sh on tests/fixtures/order-first, as docs/parallel.md S1a states: the first attempt in the ledger is at the source-earliest site. Run scripts/gate.sh: stdout is one JSON object; its steps list holds a step named 'site order by declaration coordinates' with ok true, and failed is 0.
What constraints apply? State them in plain prose. Spec and Core import no Shell module (scripts/gate.sh checks it). Termination stays a theorem in LeanMend/Spec/Termination.lean, with no retry cap and no timeout as a control. Decision D10 holds: lean-mend adds no declaration to a target. lean-mend depends on Lean core only, not on Mathlib. Every committed text is in ASD-STE100 Simplified Technical English. Run export PATH="$HOME/.elan/bin:$PATH" before a lean or lake command. Scratch files go in the gitignored .scratch/ directory, not /tmp. The worker task timeout is 3600 seconds. Do not run lean-mend on EVMLean: one EVMLean run takes about 2 hours, and the operator runs it after the merge.
Where does this apply? (e.g. gateway route, mobile screen, CLI verb) LeanMend/Spec/Types.lean, LeanMend/Core/Mend.lean, LeanMend/Shell/Target.lean, probe/Probe.lean regions
restatement: lean-mend must always work first on the error that sits earliest in the source file. Each open error site must carry the index of its declaration in source order. The Core must keep the open sites sorted by the pair (declaration index, bytes from the error to the end of that declaration). Then the head site is the source-earliest error, not the first error in Lean's message order. Today the Core keeps Lean's message order, so in EVMLean run 20 Semantics site 1040 was the head while the earlier site 288 was still open. The work builds on branch s1-partial (commit 5885691), which has the sorting code but no tests/order.sh, no tests/expose.sh and no fixture. The change is done when tests/order.sh on tests/fixtures/order-first shows the first ledger attempt at the source-earliest site, and scripts/gate.sh reports the step 'site order by declaration coordinates' ok with failed 0. Spec and Core must import no Shell module. Termination must stay a theorem in LeanMend/Spec/Termination.lean. lean-mend must depend on Lean core only, not Mathlib.
